title: The intake record
description: workareas/<workarea>/intake.json, beside backlog.json: what the ticket intake read from one fetched ticket. The intake workflow is its only writer. `tim backlog check` holds a backlog whose envelope names a ticket to it: every acceptance criterion statement is covered by a row still in play or carries the reason it is not built, every criterion of a row still to build ends with a bracket citing this ticket's statements, a repo or a ruling, and the repo keys, ids, questions and escalation follow the rules in SHAPE.md "Ticket backlogs". Rules a schema cannot hold are checked there.

ticket.description: The Jira key, copied from the fetch record sources/ticket-<key>.json, such as "EUDPA-838". It equals the backlog envelope's `ticket`.

updated.description: When Jira last updated the ticket, copied from the fetch record, such as "2026-11-25T09:00:00.000+0000".

readiness.description: The ticket's readiness, judged by the refinement check's own rules (the ticket-refiner's Verdict Guidelines).

verdict.description: The verdict. The list is the one `tim refine finalize` accepts.

reasons.description: Why, one plain sentence each. At least one.

statements.description: Everything the ticket says that the backlog must account for, numbered. Row criteria cite these ids.

repos.description: Why each repo is in the backlog: the repo key mapped to one sentence. The keys are the envelope's `repos`.

questions.description: The questions a person must answer. Minimal: a question the ticket, the code's rulings or a ruling source settles is not asked.

escalation.description: Present only when the ticket is not for this intake to build. A ticket that escalates hands over no row to build, so DISTIL or a person takes it over.

signals.description: The signals that tripped, each once.

reason.description: Why, in plain words, for the person who takes the ticket over.

text.description: Text that is not empty or only whitespace.

id.description: Upper-case letters then digits, keeping the ticket's own numbering where it has one, such as "AC1" or "SCOPE2".

kind.description: What the statement is: an acceptance criterion, a line of scope, a line of what is out of scope, or a background fact.

coveredBy.description: The ids of the backlog rows that cover it. [] when no row does.

notBuilt.description: Why no row builds it, in one sentence. An acceptance criterion with no row in play needs it.

readings.description: The readings the ticket leaves, at least two.

default.description: What gets built if nobody answers.

holdsLaunch.description: True when the build must wait for the answer. Only a cause below holds the launch.

cause.description: Why it holds the launch: security, access, data integrity, a contradiction with a signed-off scenario, or a contradiction with a rulings-ledger entry. Present when `holdsLaunch` is true, and only then.
